translations.chinese: 太史公曰：洋洋美德乎！
translations.literal: Grand Historian says: Vast and beautiful virtue!
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian says: How vast and beautiful is this virtue!

context.next: 宰制萬物，役使群眾，豈人力也哉？

translations.chinese: 宰制萬物，役使群眾，豈人力也哉？
translations.literal: Controlling ten thousand things, employing the multitudes, how is it human power?
translations.idiomatic: It controls the ten thousand things and directs the multitudes. How could this be accomplished by human power alone?

context.previous: 太史公曰：洋洋美德乎！
context.next: 余至大行禮官，觀三代損益，乃知緣人情而制禮，依人性而作儀，其所由來尚矣。

translations.chinese: 余至大行禮官，觀三代損益，乃知緣人情而制禮，依人性而作儀，其所由來尚矣。
translations.literal: I went to the Grand Procession rites official, observed the Three Dynasties' additions and subtractions, then knew that rites are established following human feelings, instruments are made relying on human nature, their origins have been ancient.
translations.idiomatic: I went to the rites office of the Grand Lineage and observed the gains and losses of the Three Dynasties. Only then did I understand that rites are established in accord with human feeling, and ritual implements are made in accord with human nature; their origin is already ancient.

context.previous: 宰制萬物，役使群眾，豈人力也哉？

translations.chinese: 人道經緯萬端，規矩無所不貫，誘進以仁義，束縛以刑罰，故德厚者位尊，祿重者寵榮，所以總一海內而整齊萬民也。
translations.literal: Human way weaves ten thousand ends, rules and squares penetrate everything, entice forward with benevolence righteousness, bind with punishments, therefore virtue thick ones position honored, emolument heavy ones favor glorious, thus unifying the realm within the seas and orderly arranging the ten thousand people.
translations.idiomatic: Human affairs weave through ten thousand strands, and rules and standards reach everywhere. People are led forward with benevolence and righteousness and bound with punishments; thus those of deep virtue are honored, and those with heavy emoluments are favored. This is how the realm within the seas is unified and the people brought into order.

context.next: 人體安駕乘，為之金輿錯衡以繁其飾；

translations.literal: Human body at ease riding driving, for it gold carriage inlaid yoke to multiply its ornaments;
translations.idiomatic: The human body finds ease in riding and driving, so it is furnished with gold carriages and inlaid yokes to enrich their adornment.

translations.literal: Following law guarding upright ones seen insulted by the world, extravagant overflowing presumptuous differing ones called manifest glory.
translations.idiomatic: Those who follow the law and guard uprightness are mocked by the world, while those who are extravagant, excessive, and presumptuous are called illustrious and glorious.

translations.literal: Even Zi Xia, disciples' high disciple, still said "Going out seeing variegated splendor flourishing beauty and pleased, entering hearing Master Dao and happy, two things heart battle, unable self-decide", moreover middle ordinary and below, gradually immersed in lost teaching, clothed in established customs?
translations.idiomatic: Even Zi Xia, the highest disciple among the disciples, still said: 'Going out I see variegated splendor and flourishing beauty and am pleased; entering I hear the Master's Dao and am happy. These two things battle in my heart, and I cannot decide for myself.' How much more so for those of middle and ordinary ability and below, who are gradually immersed in lost teaching and clothed in established customs?

translations.idiomatic: Confucius said: 'It must be rectifying names.' In Wei, however, this did not fit where he was staying.

translations.literal: Zhong Ni passed away after, received teachings disciples sunken submerged not raised, some went to Qi, Chu, some entered rivers seas, how not painful!
translations.idiomatic: After Zhongni passed away, his disciples who received his teachings sank into obscurity and were not raised up. Some went to Qi and Chu, others entered the rivers and seas. How could this not be painful!

context.previous: 孔子曰「必也正名」，於衛所居不合。

translations.idiomatic: When Qin possessed the realm, it entirely took in the rites and ceremonies of the six states, selecting what was good from them. Though they did not match the sage system, they honored the ruler and suppressed ministers, and the court was flourishing and orderly, following ancient practices.

translations.idiomatic: As for Gaozu, who shone over All under Heaven, Shusun Tong made considerable additions and subtractions, but in broad outline he still followed the old Qin practices.

translations.literal: Filial Wen ascended throne, officials discussed wished establish ceremony rites, Filial Wen fond Daoist learning, considered elaborate rites decorated appearances, no benefit to governing, personal transformation what ear, therefore dismissed them.
translations.idiomatic: When Filial Wen ascended the throne, the officials discussed and wished to establish ceremony and rites. But Filial Wen was fond of Daoist learning and considered that elaborate rites and decorated appearances were of no benefit to governing—what mattered was personal transformation—so he dismissed them.

translations.idiomatic: The human condition involves desires. If desires are not fulfilled, one cannot be without resentment. If resentment has no measure, then there is contention. If there is contention, then there is chaos.

translations.idiomatic: The former kings hated this chaos, so they established rites and righteousness to nourish people's desires and supply their requests, ensuring that desires do not exhaust things and things do not bend to desires. The two mutually await and grow—this is the origin of rites.

translations.chinese: 疏房床笫几席，所以養體也：故禮者養也。
translations.literal: Spacious rooms beds mats tables mats, thus nourish body also: therefore rites are nourishment.
translations.idiomatic: Spacious rooms, beds, mats, tables, and seating mats thus nourish the body. Therefore, rites are nourishment.

context.previous: 刻鏤文章，所以養目也；

translations.chinese: 君子既得其養，又好其辨也。
translations.literal: Superior man already obtained its nourishment, moreover likes its distinction.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman has already obtained its nourishment, and moreover likes its distinction.

context.next: 所謂辨者，貴賤有等，長少有差，貧富輕重皆有稱也。

translations.chinese: 所謂辨者，貴賤有等，長少有差，貧富輕重皆有稱也。
translations.literal: What is called distinction, noble base have ranks, elder younger have differences, poor rich light heavy all have proportion.
translations.idiomatic: What is called distinction means that the noble and the base have ranks, the elder and the younger have differences, and the poor and the rich, the light and the heavy all have their proper proportions.

context.previous: 君子既得其養，又好其辨也。
context.next: 故天子大路越席，所以養體也；

translations.chinese: 故天子大路越席，所以養體也；
translations.literal: Therefore Son of Heaven great carriage rush mats, thus nourish body also;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, the Son of Heaven's great carriage with rush mats thus nourishes the body.

context.previous: 所謂辨者，貴賤有等，長少有差，貧富輕重皆有稱也。
context.next: 側載臭茝，所以養鼻也；

translations.chinese: 側載臭茝，所以養鼻也；
translations.literal: Side loaded fragrant chai, thus nourish nose also;
translations.idiomatic: Side panels loaded with fragrant chai thus nourish the nose.

context.previous: 故天子大路越席，所以養體也；
context.next: 前有錯衡，所以養目也；

translations.chinese: 前有錯衡，所以養目也；
translations.literal: Front has inlaid yoke, thus nourish eyes also;
translations.idiomatic: The front has an inlaid yoke, thus nourishing the eyes.

context.previous: 側載臭茝，所以養鼻也；
context.next: 和鸞之聲，步中武象，驟中韶濩，所以養耳也；

translations.chinese: 和鸞之聲，步中武象，驟中韶濩，所以養耳也；
translations.literal: Harmonious luan sound, walking matches Wu image, galloping matches Shao Hu, thus nourish ears also;
translations.idiomatic: The harmonious sound of luan bells, walking that matches the image of Wu, galloping that matches Shao and Hu—these thus nourish the ears.

context.previous: 前有錯衡，所以養目也；
context.next: 龍旂九斿，所以養信也；

translations.chinese: 龍旂九斿，所以養信也；
translations.literal: Dragon banner nine streamers, thus nourish trustworthiness also;
translations.idiomatic: The dragon banner with nine streamers thus nourishes trustworthiness.

context.previous: 和鸞之聲，步中武象，驟中韶濩，所以養耳也；
context.next: 寢兕持虎，鮫韅彌龍，所以養威也。

translations.chinese: 寢兕持虎，鮫韅彌龍，所以養威也。
translations.literal: Reclining rhinoceros grasping tiger, shark boots dragon-embroidered, thus nourish awe also.
translations.idiomatic: Reclining rhinoceroses and grasping tigers, the shark-skin boots embroidered with dragons—these thus nourish awe.

context.previous: 龍旂九斿，所以養信也；
context.next: 故大路之馬，必信至教順，然後乘之，所以養安也。

translations.chinese: 故大路之馬，必信至教順，然後乘之，所以養安也。
translations.literal: Therefore great carriage's horses, must trustworthy arrive trained obedient, then ride them, thus nourish security also.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, the horses of the great carriage must be trustworthy, arrive well-trained and obedient, and only then are they ridden. This thus nourishes security.

context.previous: 寢兕持虎，鮫韅彌龍，所以養威也。
context.next: 孰知夫［士］出死要節之所以養生也。

translations.chinese: 孰知夫［士］出死要節之所以養生也。
translations.literal: Who knows that shi exiting death demanding integrity reason for nourishing life.
translations.idiomatic: Who knows that the scholar's willingness to face death and demand integrity is the very reason for nourishing life?

context.previous: 故大路之馬，必信至教順，然後乘之，所以養安也。
context.next: 孰知夫輕費用之所以養財也，孰知夫恭敬辭讓之所以養安也，孰知夫禮義文理之所以養情也。

translations.chinese: 孰知夫輕費用之所以養財也，孰知夫恭敬辭讓之所以養安也，孰知夫禮義文理之所以養情也。
translations.literal: Who knows that light expenditure reason for nourishing wealth, who knows that respectful yielding reason for nourishing security, who knows that rites righteousness pattern principle reason for nourishing feelings.
translations.idiomatic: Who knows that frugal expenditure is the reason for nourishing wealth? Who knows that respectful yielding is the reason for nourishing security? Who knows that rites, righteousness, patterns, and principles are the reason for nourishing feelings?

context.previous: 孰知夫［士］出死要節之所以養生也。

translations.chinese: 人茍生之為見，若者必死；
translations.literal: Person if birth's as seen, such ones must die;
translations.idiomatic: If a person views mere survival as the goal, such people must die.

context.next: 茍利之為見，若者必害；

translations.chinese: 茍利之為見，若者必害；
translations.literal: If profit's as seen, such ones must harm;
translations.idiomatic: If profit is viewed as the goal, such people must come to harm.

context.previous: 人茍生之為見，若者必死；
context.next: 怠惰之為安，若者必危；

translations.chinese: 怠惰之為安，若者必危；
translations.literal: Indolent lazy as security, such ones must danger;
translations.idiomatic: If indolence and laziness are viewed as security, such people must come to danger.

context.previous: 茍利之為見，若者必害；
context.next: 情勝之為安，若者必滅。

translations.chinese: 情勝之為安，若者必滅。
translations.literal: Emotions victory as security, such ones must extinction.
translations.idiomatic: If victory of emotions is viewed as security, such people must come to extinction.

context.previous: 怠惰之為安，若者必危；
context.next: 故聖人一之於禮義，則兩得之矣；

translations.chinese: 故聖人一之於禮義，則兩得之矣；
translations.literal: Therefore sages unify at rites righteousness, then both obtain them;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, when sages unify things through rites and righteousness, they obtain both benefits.

context.previous: 情勝之為安，若者必滅。
context.next: 一之於情性，則兩失之矣。

translations.chinese: 一之於情性，則兩失之矣。
translations.literal: Unify at emotions nature, then both lose them.
translations.idiomatic: When they unify things through emotions and nature, they lose both benefits.

context.previous: 故聖人一之於禮義，則兩得之矣；
context.next: 故儒者將使人兩得之者也，墨者將使人兩失之者也。

translations.chinese: 故儒者將使人兩得之者也，墨者將使人兩失之者也。
translations.literal: Therefore Confucian scholars will make people both obtain them, Mohist scholars will make people both lose them.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, the Confucian scholars will enable people to obtain both benefits, while the Mohist scholars will cause people to lose both benefits.

context.previous: 一之於情性，則兩失之矣。
context.next: 是儒墨之分。

translations.chinese: 是儒墨之分。
translations.literal: This is Confucian Mohist division.
translations.idiomatic: This is the division between Confucians and Mohists.

context.previous: 故儒者將使人兩得之者也，墨者將使人兩失之者也。

translations.chinese: 治辨之極也，彊固之本也，威行之道也，功名之總也。
translations.literal: Order distinction's extreme, strong solid foundation, awe implementation way, merit fame summary.
translations.idiomatic: It is the extreme of order and distinction, the foundation of strength and solidity, the way to implement awe, and the summary of merit and fame.

context.next: 王公由之，所以一天下，臣諸侯也；

translations.chinese: 王公由之，所以一天下，臣諸侯也；
translations.literal: Kings dukes follow it, thus unify realm, make ministers of feudal lords;
translations.idiomatic: When kings and dukes follow it, they thus unify the realm and make ministers of the feudal lords.

context.previous: 治辨之極也，彊固之本也，威行之道也，功名之總也。
context.next: 弗由之，所以捐社稷也。

translations.chinese: 弗由之，所以捐社稷也。
translations.literal: Not follow it, thus abandon altars grain.
translations.idiomatic: If they do not follow it, they thus abandon the altars of soil and grain.

context.previous: 王公由之，所以一天下，臣諸侯也；
context.next: 故堅革利兵不足以為勝，高城深池不足以為固，嚴令繁刑不足以為威。

translations.chinese: 故堅革利兵不足以為勝，高城深池不足以為固，嚴令繁刑不足以為威。
translations.literal: Therefore tough armor sharp weapons insufficient for victory, high walls deep moats insufficient for security, strict orders numerous punishments insufficient for awe.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, the tough armor and sharp weapons are insufficient for victory; the high walls and deep moats are insufficient for security; the strict orders and numerous punishments are insufficient for awe.

context.previous: 弗由之，所以捐社稷也。
context.next: 由其道則行，不由其道則廢。

translations.chinese: 由其道則行，不由其道則廢。
translations.literal: Follow its way then proceed, not follow its way then abandon.
translations.idiomatic: If you follow its way, then you proceed; if you do not follow its way, then you are abandoned.

context.previous: 故堅革利兵不足以為勝，高城深池不足以為固，嚴令繁刑不足以為威。
context.next: 楚人鮫革犀兕，所以為甲，堅如金石；

translations.chinese: 楚人鮫革犀兕，所以為甲，堅如金石；
translations.literal: Chu people shark hide rhinoceros buffalo, thus make armor, hard like metal stone;
translations.idiomatic: The people of Chu used shark hide, rhinoceros hide, and buffalo hide to make armor as hard as metal and stone.

context.previous: 由其道則行，不由其道則廢。
context.next: 宛之鉅鐵施，鉆如蜂蠆，輕利剽遫，卒如熛風。

translations.chinese: 宛之鉅鐵施，鉆如蜂蠆，輕利剽遫，卒如熛風。
translations.literal: Wan great iron spears, sharp like bee scorpion, light advantageous swift speedy, troops like blazing wind.
translations.idiomatic: The great iron spears from Wan were as sharp as bees and scorpions, light and advantageous, swift and speedy—their troops were like a blazing wind.

context.previous: 楚人鮫革犀兕，所以為甲，堅如金石；
context.next: 然而兵殆於垂涉，唐昧死焉；

translations.chinese: 然而兵殆於垂涉，唐昧死焉；
translations.literal: However troops endangered at Chui She, Tang Mei died there;
translations.idiomatic: However, their troops were endangered at Chui and She, and Tang Mei died there.

context.previous: 宛之鉅鐵施，鉆如蜂蠆，輕利剽遫，卒如熛風。
context.next: 莊蹻起，楚分而為四參。

translations.chinese: 莊蹻起，楚分而為四參。
translations.literal: Zhuang Qiao arose, Chu divided became four portions.
translations.idiomatic: Zhuang Qiao arose, and Chu was divided into four portions.

context.previous: 然而兵殆於垂涉，唐昧死焉；
context.next: 是豈無堅革利兵哉？

translations.chinese: 是豈無堅革利兵哉？
translations.literal: This how without tough armor sharp weapons?
translations.idiomatic: How could this be without tough armor and sharp weapons?

context.previous: 莊蹻起，楚分而為四參。
context.next: 其所以統之者非其道故也。

translations.chinese: 其所以統之者非其道故也。
translations.literal: Their way of controlling them not its way therefore.
translations.idiomatic: It was because their way of controlling them was not the proper way.

context.previous: 是豈無堅革利兵哉？
context.next: 汝潁以為險，江漢以為池，阻之以鄧林，緣之以方城。

translations.chinese: 汝潁以為險，江漢以為池，阻之以鄧林，緣之以方城。
translations.literal: Ru Ying as danger, Jiang Han as moat, blocked by Deng forest, bordered by Fang city.
translations.idiomatic: They considered the Ru and Ying as dangers, the Jiang and Han as moats, blocked themselves with the Deng forest, and bordered themselves with Fangcheng.

context.previous: 其所以統之者非其道故也。
context.next: 然而秦師至鄢郢，舉若振槁。

translations.chinese: 然而秦師至鄢郢，舉若振槁。
translations.literal: However Qin armies reached Yan Ying, took like shaking withered.
translations.idiomatic: However, when the Qin armies reached Yan and Ying, they took them as easily as shaking withered grass.

context.previous: 汝潁以為險，江漢以為池，阻之以鄧林，緣之以方城。
context.next: 是豈無固塞險阻哉？

translations.chinese: 是豈無固塞險阻哉？
translations.literal: This how without solid barriers dangerous obstacles?
translations.idiomatic: How could this be without solid barriers and dangerous obstacles?

context.previous: 然而秦師至鄢郢，舉若振槁。
context.next: 其所以統之者非其道故也。

translations.chinese: 其所以統之者非其道故也。
translations.literal: Their way of controlling them not its way therefore.
translations.idiomatic: It was because their way of controlling them was not the proper way.

context.previous: 是豈無固塞險阻哉？
context.next: 紂剖比干，囚箕子，為炮格，刑殺無辜，時臣下懔然，莫必其命。

translations.chinese: 紂剖比干，囚箕子，為炮格，刑殺無辜，時臣下懔然，莫必其命。
translations.literal: Zhou cut open Bi Gan, imprisoned Ji Zi, made pao ge, punished killed innocent, time ministers below fearful, none certain their fate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou disemboweled Bi Gan, imprisoned Ji Zi, made the pao ge, and punished and killed the innocent. At that time, the ministers below were terrified, and none were certain of their fate.

context.previous: 其所以統之者非其道故也。
context.next: 然而周師至，而令不行乎下，不能用其民。

translations.chinese: 然而周師至，而令不行乎下，不能用其民。
translations.literal: However Zhou armies arrived, yet commands not proceed below, cannot use their people.
translations.idiomatic: However, when the Zhou armies arrived, commands did not proceed below, and they could not employ their people.

context.previous: 紂剖比干，囚箕子，為炮格，刑殺無辜，時臣下懔然，莫必其命。
context.next: 是豈令不嚴，刑不陖哉？

translations.chinese: 是豈令不嚴，刑不陖哉？
translations.literal: This how commands not strict, punishments not numerous?
translations.idiomatic: How could this be because the commands were not strict and the punishments not numerous?

context.previous: 然而周師至，而令不行乎下，不能用其民。
context.next: 其所以統之者非其道故也。

translations.chinese: 其所以統之者非其道故也。
translations.literal: Their way of controlling them not its way therefore.
translations.idiomatic: It was because their way of controlling them was not the proper way.

context.previous: 是豈令不嚴，刑不陖哉？

translations.chinese: 古者之兵，戈矛弓矢而已，然而敵國不待試而詘。
translations.literal: Ancient ones' weapons, dagger-axes spears bows arrows only, however enemy states not wait test and submit.
translations.idiomatic: The weapons of the ancients were only dagger-axes, spears, bows, and arrows, yet enemy states did not wait to be tested before submitting.

context.next: 城郭不集，溝池不掘，固塞不樹，機變不張，然而國晏然不畏外而固者，無他故焉，明道而均分之，時使而誠愛之，則下應之如景響。

translations.chinese: 城郭不集，溝池不掘，固塞不樹，機變不張，然而國晏然不畏外而固者，無他故焉，明道而均分之，時使而誠愛之，則下應之如景響。
translations.literal: Walls cities not gathered, moats pools not dug, solid barriers not planted, stratagems changes not displayed, however state peaceful not fear external secure, no other reason, clarify way evenly distribute them, timely employ sincerely love them, then below respond like shadow echo.
translations.idiomatic: Walls and cities are not gathered, moats and pools are not dug, solid barriers are not planted, and stratagems and changes are not displayed. Yet the state is peaceful, does not fear the external, and is secure. There is no other reason: clarify the way and distribute evenly; employ them timely and love them sincerely, and then those below will respond like a shadow to an echo.

context.previous: 古者之兵，戈矛弓矢而已，然而敵國不待試而詘。
context.next: 有不由命者，然後俟之以刑，則民知罪矣。

translations.chinese: 有不由命者，然後俟之以刑，則民知罪矣。
translations.literal: Have not follow commands, then wait with punishments, then people know crime.
translations.idiomatic: For those who do not follow commands, then await them with punishments, and the people will know their crimes.

context.previous: 城郭不集，溝池不掘，固塞不樹，機變不張，然而國晏然不畏外而固者，無他故焉，明道而均分之，時使而誠愛之，則下應之如景響。
context.next: 故刑一人而天下服。

translations.chinese: 故刑一人而天下服。
translations.literal: Therefore punish one person and realm submits.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, punish one person and the realm submits.

context.previous: 有不由命者，然後俟之以刑，則民知罪矣。
context.next: 罪人不尤其上，知罪之在己也。

translations.chinese: 罪人不尤其上，知罪之在己也。
translations.literal: Criminal people not blame superiors, know crime in themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Criminals do not blame their superiors; they know the crime is in themselves.

context.previous: 故刑一人而天下服。
context.next: 是故刑罰省而威行如流，無他故焉，由其道故也。

translations.chinese: 是故刑罰省而威行如流，無他故焉，由其道故也。
translations.literal: Therefore punishments few awe flows like stream, no other reason, by its way therefore.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, punishments are few and awe flows like a stream. There is no other reason; it is because of its way.

context.previous: 罪人不尤其上，知罪之在己也。
context.next: 故由其道則行，不由其道則廢。

translations.chinese: 故由其道則行，不由其道則廢。
translations.literal: Therefore follow its way then proceed, not follow its way then abandon.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, if you follow its way, then you proceed; if you do not follow its way, then you are abandoned.

context.previous: 是故刑罰省而威行如流，無他故焉，由其道故也。
context.next: 古者帝堯之治天下也，蓋殺一人刑二人而天下治。

translations.chinese: 古者帝堯之治天下也，蓋殺一人刑二人而天下治。
translations.literal: Ancient Emperor Yao governed realm, probably killed one person punished two persons and realm governed.
translations.idiomatic: When the ancient Emperor Yao governed the realm, he probably killed one person and punished two persons, and the realm was governed.

context.previous: 故由其道則行，不由其道則廢。
context.next: 傳曰「威厲而不試，刑措而不用」。

translations.chinese: 傳曰「威厲而不試，刑措而不用」。
translations.literal: Tradition says "Awe severe not tested, punishments set aside not used".
translations.idiomatic: The tradition says: 'Awe is severe but not tested; punishments are set aside and not used.'

context.previous: 古者帝堯之治天下也，蓋殺一人刑二人而天下治。

translations.chinese: 天地者，生之本也；
translations.literal: Heaven earth, life root;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth are the root of life.

context.next: 先祖者，類之本也；

translations.chinese: 先祖者，類之本也；
translations.literal: Forefathers, kind root;
translations.idiomatic: Forefathers are the root of the kind.

context.previous: 天地者，生之本也；
context.next: 君師者，治之本也。

translations.chinese: 君師者，治之本也。
translations.literal: Lord teacher, governance root.
translations.idiomatic: The lord and teacher are the root of governance.

context.previous: 先祖者，類之本也；
context.next: 無天地惡生？

translations.chinese: 無天地惡生？
translations.literal: Without heaven earth hate life?
translations.idiomatic: Without heaven and earth, who would hate life?

context.previous: 君師者，治之本也。
context.next: 無先祖惡出？

translations.chinese: 無先祖惡出？
translations.literal: Without forefathers hate birth?
translations.idiomatic: Without forefathers, who would hate birth?

context.previous: 無天地惡生？
context.next: 無君師惡治？

translations.chinese: 無君師惡治？
translations.literal: Without lord teacher hate governance?
translations.idiomatic: Without lord and teacher, who would hate governance?

context.previous: 無先祖惡出？
context.next: 三者偏亡，則無安人。

translations.chinese: 三者偏亡，則無安人。
translations.literal: Three things partially lost, then no secure people.
translations.idiomatic: If any of the three is partially lost, then there are no secure people.

context.previous: 無君師惡治？
context.next: 故禮，上事天，下事地，尊先祖而隆君師，是禮之三本也。

translations.chinese: 故禮，上事天，下事地，尊先祖而隆君師，是禮之三本也。
translations.literal: Therefore rites, above serve heaven, below serve earth, honor forefathers elevate lord teacher, this rites' three roots.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, rites serve heaven above and earth below, honor the forefathers and elevate the lord and teacher—these are the three roots of rites.

context.previous: 三者偏亡，則無安人。

translations.chinese: 故王者天太祖，諸侯不敢懷，大夫士有常宗，所以辨貴賤。
translations.literal: Therefore kings regard heaven great ancestor, feudal lords not dare harbor, grandees scholars have constant ancestor, thus distinguish noble base.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, kings regard heaven as their great ancestor; feudal lords do not dare harbor resentment; grandees and scholars have constant ancestors—this is to distinguish the noble and the base.

context.next: 貴賤治，得之本也。

translations.chinese: 貴賤治，得之本也。
translations.literal: Noble base ordered, obtain root.
translations.idiomatic: When the noble and the base are brought into order, that is the root of order.

context.previous: 故王者天太祖，諸侯不敢懷，大夫士有常宗，所以辨貴賤。

translations.chinese: 郊疇乎天子，社至乎諸侯，函及士大夫，所以辨尊者事尊，卑者事卑，宜鉅者鉅，宜小者小。
translations.literal: Suburban sacrifice to Son of Heaven, altar sacrifice to feudal lords, include down to grandees scholars, thus distinguish honored serve honored, lowly serve lowly, suitable great great, suitable small small.
translations.idiomatic: The suburban sacrifice goes to the Son of Heaven; the sacrifice to the altars of soil and grain goes to the feudal lords; it extends down to the grandees and scholars, so that the honored serve the honored, the lowly serve the lowly, and what should be great is great, what should be small is small.

translations.chinese: 故有天下者事七世，有一國者事五世，有五乘之地者事三世，有三乘之地者事二世，有特牲而食者不得立宗廟，所以辨積厚者流澤廣，積薄者流澤狹也。
translations.literal: Therefore possess realm serve seven generations, possess one state serve five generations, possess five chariot land serve three generations, possess three chariot land serve two generations, have special sacrifice eat not obtain establish ancestral temple, thus distinguish accumulation thick flow grace broad, accumulation thin flow grace narrow.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, one who possesses All under Heaven serves seven generations; one who possesses a state serves five generations; one with land for five chariots serves three generations; one with land for three chariots serves two generations; one who has only a special sacrifice to eat may not establish an ancestral temple. This is to distinguish that thick accumulation flows with broad blessing, and thin accumulation with narrow blessing.

translations.chinese: 大饗上玄尊，俎上腥魚，先大羹，貴食飲之本也。
translations.literal: Great feast above mysterious honor, stand above raw fish, first great broth, noble food drink root.
translations.idiomatic: In the great feast, the mysterious vessel is placed above and raw fish is set on the stand; the great broth comes first. This is to honor the root of food and drink.

translations.chinese: 大饗上玄尊而用薄酒，食先黍稷而飯稻粱，祭嚌先大羹而飽庶羞，貴本而親用也。
translations.literal: Great feast above mysterious honor use thin wine, food first millet panicled millet rice polished rice, sacrifice taste first great broth satiate many delicacies, noble root intimate use.
translations.idiomatic: In the great feast, the mysterious vessel is placed above and thin wine is used; food begins with millet and panicled millet, then rice and polished rice; in sacrifice and tasting, the great broth comes first and one is filled with the many offerings. This is to honor the root and to treat things as close at hand.

context.next: 貴本之謂文，親用之謂理，兩者合而成文，以歸太一，是謂大隆。

translations.chinese: 貴本之謂文，親用之謂理，兩者合而成文，以歸太一，是謂大隆。
translations.literal: Noble root called pattern, intimate use called principle, two combine become pattern, to return great one, this called great flourishing.
translations.idiomatic: Honoring the root is called pattern; treating things as close at hand is called principle. The two join and become pattern, returning to the Great One; this is called great flourishing.

context.previous: 大饗上玄尊而用薄酒，食先黍稷而飯稻粱，祭嚌先大羹而飽庶羞，貴本而親用也。

translations.chinese: 故尊之上玄尊也，俎之上腥魚也，豆之先大羹，一也。
translations.literal: Therefore honor above mysterious honor, stand above raw fish, bowl first great broth, one.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, the mysterious vessel is above in the honor vessel; raw fish is above on the stand; the great broth comes first in the bowl—they are one.

translations.chinese: 利爵弗啐也，成事俎弗嘗也，三侑之弗食也。
translations.literal: Beneficial wine not sip, completed affairs stand not taste, three toasts not eat.
translations.idiomatic: The beneficial wine is not sipped; the completed offering on the stand is not tasted; the three libations are not eaten.

translations.chinese: 大昏之未廢齊也，大廟之未內尸也，始絕之未小斂，一也。
translations.literal: Great marriage not yet abolish fast, great temple not yet enter corpse, beginning mourning not yet small dressing, one.
translations.idiomatic: The great marriage has not yet ended the fast; the great temple has not yet admitted the corpse; the beginning of mourning has not yet reached the small dressing—they are one.

translations.chinese: 大路之素幬也，郊之麻絻，喪服之先散麻，一也。
translations.literal: Great carriage plain canopy, suburban hemp cap, mourning garments first scattered hemp, one.
translations.idiomatic: The great carriage has its plain canopy; the suburban sacrifice has its hemp cap; mourning garments begin with scattered hemp—they are one.

translations.chinese: 三年哭之不反也，清廟之歌一倡而三嘆，縣一鐘尚拊膈，朱弦而通越，一也。
translations.literal: Three years weeping not return, pure temple song one lead three sigh, hang one bell still pat frame, vermilion strings pass zither, one.
translations.idiomatic: The three-year weeping does not return; the song of the Pure Temple has one leading voice and three responding sighs; a single bell is hung and still beats against the breast; vermilion strings cross the zither—they are one.

translations.chinese: 凡禮始乎脫，成乎文，終乎稅。
translations.literal: All rites begin with removal, complete with pattern, end with return.
translations.idiomatic: All rites begin with removal, complete with pattern, and end with return.

context.next: 故至備，情文俱盡；

translations.chinese: 故至備，情文俱盡；
translations.literal: Therefore utmost preparation, feelings patterns both exhausted;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, at the highest level, feeling and pattern are both fully exhausted.

context.previous: 凡禮始乎脫，成乎文，終乎稅。
context.next: 其次，情文代勝；

translations.chinese: 其次，情文代勝；
translations.literal: Next, feelings patterns alternate victory;
translations.idiomatic: Next, feeling and pattern alternate in predominance.

context.previous: 故至備，情文俱盡；
context.next: 其下，復情以歸太一。

translations.chinese: 其下，復情以歸太一。
translations.literal: Below that, return feelings to return great one.
translations.idiomatic: At the lowest level, feeling is restored and returned to the Great One.

context.previous: 其次，情文代勝；

translations.chinese: 天地以合，日月以明，四時以序，星辰以行，江河以流，萬物以昌，好惡以節，喜怒以當。
translations.literal: Heaven earth thus unite, sun moon thus bright, four seasons thus ordered, stars constellations thus move, rivers thus flow, ten thousand things thus flourish, likes dislikes thus regulated, joy anger thus appropriate.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven and earth thus unite; the sun and moon thus shine; the four seasons thus follow in order; the stars and constellations thus move; the rivers thus flow; the ten thousand things thus flourish; likes and dislikes are moderated; joy and anger are made fitting.

context.next: 以為下則順，以為上則明。

translations.chinese: 以為下則順，以為上則明。
translations.literal: Use as below then compliant, use as above then clear.
translations.idiomatic: When used below, they are compliant; when used above, they are illuminating.

context.previous: 天地以合，日月以明，四時以序，星辰以行，江河以流，萬物以昌，好惡以節，喜怒以當。

translations.chinese: 太史公曰：至矣哉！
translations.literal: Grand Historian says: Utmost!
translations.idiomatic: The Grand Historian says: 'How perfect!'

context.next: 立隆以為極，而天下莫之能益損也。

translations.chinese: 立隆以為極，而天下莫之能益損也。
translations.literal: Establish flourishing as extreme, and realm none able increase decrease it.
translations.idiomatic: They establish flourishing as the highest point, and All under Heaven can neither add to it nor subtract from it.

context.previous: 太史公曰：至矣哉！
context.next: 本末相順，終始相應，至文有以辨，至察有以說。

translations.chinese: 本末相順，終始相應，至文有以辨，至察有以說。
translations.literal: Root tip mutually compliant, end beginning mutually respond, utmost pattern has to distinguish, utmost discernment has to explain.
translations.idiomatic: Root and tip move in mutual sequence; end and beginning answer each other. At the highest point of pattern, there is what allows distinction; at the highest point of discernment, there is what allows explanation.

context.previous: 立隆以為極，而天下莫之能益損也。
context.next: 天下從之者治，不從者亂；

translations.chinese: 天下從之者治，不從者亂；
translations.literal: Realm follow it ordered, not follow chaotic;
translations.idiomatic: Those in All under Heaven who follow it are ordered; those who do not follow it are in disorder.

context.previous: 本末相順，終始相應，至文有以辨，至察有以說。
context.next: 從之者安，不從者危。

translations.chinese: 從之者安，不從者危。
translations.literal: Follow it secure, not follow dangerous.
translations.idiomatic: Those who follow it are secure; those who do not follow it are in danger.

context.previous: 天下從之者治，不從者亂；
context.next: 小人不能則也。

translations.chinese: 小人不能則也。
translations.literal: Small people cannot follow it.
translations.idiomatic: Small people cannot follow it.

context.previous: 從之者安，不從者危。

translations.chinese: 禮之貌誠深矣，堅白同異之察，入焉而弱。
translations.literal: Rites appearance truly deep, hard white same different discernment, enter therein weak.
translations.idiomatic: The appearance of rites is truly profound; the distinctions made by the hard and white, the same and the different, enter there and grow weak.

context.next: 其貌誠大矣，擅作典制褊陋之說，入焉而望。

translations.chinese: 其貌誠大矣，擅作典制褊陋之說，入焉而望。
translations.literal: Its appearance truly great, monopolize make standards narrow petty theories, enter therein gaze.
translations.idiomatic: Its appearance is truly great; the theories of monopolizing the making of standards and of narrow pettiness enter there and are lost.

context.previous: 禮之貌誠深矣，堅白同異之察，入焉而弱。
context.next: 其貌誠高矣，暴慢恣睢，輕俗以為高之屬，入焉而隊。

translations.chinese: 其貌誠高矣，暴慢恣睢，輕俗以為高之屬，入焉而隊。
translations.literal: Its appearance truly high, violent arrogant unrestrained, despise customs as high category, enter therein fall.
translations.idiomatic: Its appearance is truly lofty; those who are violent, arrogant, and unrestrained, and who despise custom as a mark of loftiness, enter there and fall.

context.previous: 其貌誠大矣，擅作典制褊陋之說，入焉而望。
context.next: 故繩誠陳，則不可欺以曲直；

translations.chinese: 故繩誠陳，則不可欺以曲直；
translations.literal: Therefore cord truly displayed, then cannot cheat with crooked straight;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, if the cord is truly stretched out, one cannot deceive it with crooked or straight.

context.previous: 其貌誠高矣，暴慢恣睢，輕俗以為高之屬，入焉而隊。
context.next: 衡誠縣，則不可欺以輕重；

translations.chinese: 衡誠縣，則不可欺以輕重；
translations.literal: Balance truly hung, then cannot cheat with light heavy;
translations.idiomatic: If the balance is truly suspended, one cannot deceive it with light or heavy.

context.previous: 故繩誠陳，則不可欺以曲直；
context.next: 規矩誠錯，則不可欺以方員；

translations.chinese: 規矩誠錯，則不可欺以方員；
translations.literal: Compass square truly set, then cannot cheat with square round;
translations.idiomatic: If the compass and square are truly set, one cannot deceive them with square or round.

context.previous: 衡誠縣，則不可欺以輕重；
context.next: 君子審禮，則不可欺以詐偽。

translations.chinese: 君子審禮，則不可欺以詐偽。
translations.literal: Superior man examines rites, then cannot cheat with deceit falsehood.
translations.idiomatic: If the gentleman examines rites, he cannot be deceived by deceit or falsehood.

context.previous: 規矩誠錯，則不可欺以方員；
context.next: 故繩者，直之至也；

translations.chinese: 故繩者，直之至也；
translations.literal: Therefore cord is straight utmost;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, the cord is the utmost of straightness.

context.previous: 君子審禮，則不可欺以詐偽。
context.next: 衡者，平之至也；

translations.chinese: 衡者，平之至也；
translations.literal: Balance is level utmost;
translations.idiomatic: The balance is the utmost of levelness.

context.previous: 故繩者，直之至也；
context.next: 規矩者，方員之至也；

translations.chinese: 規矩者，方員之至也；
translations.literal: Compass square is square round utmost;
translations.idiomatic: The compass and square are the utmost of square and round.

context.previous: 衡者，平之至也；
context.next: 禮者，人道之極也。

translations.chinese: 禮者，人道之極也。
translations.literal: Rites are human way extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Rites are the apex of the human way.

context.previous: 規矩者，方員之至也；
context.next: 然而不法禮者不足禮，謂之無方之民；

translations.chinese: 然而不法禮者不足禮，謂之無方之民；
translations.literal: However not model rites insufficient rites, called directionless people;
translations.idiomatic: However, those who do not model themselves on the rites are not fit for rites; they are called people without direction.

context.previous: 禮者，人道之極也。
context.next: 法禮足禮，謂之有方之士。

translations.chinese: 法禮足禮，謂之有方之士。
translations.literal: Model rites sufficient rites, called directed scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Those who model themselves on the rites and are fully fit for rites are called men of direction.

context.previous: 然而不法禮者不足禮，謂之無方之民；
context.next: 禮之中，能思索，謂之能慮；

translations.chinese: 禮之中，能思索，謂之能慮；
translations.literal: Ritual midst, able ponder, called able consider;
translations.idiomatic: Within rites, those who can ponder are called capable of deliberation.

context.previous: 法禮足禮，謂之有方之士。
context.next: 能慮勿易，謂之能固。

translations.chinese: 能慮勿易，謂之能固。
translations.literal: Able consider not change, called able firm.
translations.idiomatic: Those who can deliberate without changing are called capable of firmness.

context.previous: 禮之中，能思索，謂之能慮；
context.next: 能慮能固，加好之焉，聖矣。

translations.chinese: 能慮能固，加好之焉，聖矣。
translations.literal: Able consider able firm, add like it there, sage.
translations.idiomatic: Those who can deliberate and be firm, and add a liking for them, are sages.

context.previous: 能慮勿易，謂之能固。
context.next: 天者，高之極也；

translations.chinese: 天者，高之極也；
translations.literal: Heaven is high extreme;
translations.idiomatic: Heaven is the highest point of height.

context.previous: 能慮能固，加好之焉，聖矣。
context.next: 地者，下之極也；

translations.chinese: 地者，下之極也；
translations.literal: Earth is low extreme;
translations.idiomatic: Earth is the highest point of depth.

context.previous: 天者，高之極也；
context.next: 日月者，明之極也；

translations.chinese: 日月者，明之極也；
translations.literal: Sun moon are brightness extreme;
translations.idiomatic: The sun and moon are the highest point of brightness.

context.previous: 地者，下之極也；
context.next: 無窮者，廣大之極也；

translations.chinese: 無窮者，廣大之極也；
translations.literal: Infinite is vast great extreme;
translations.idiomatic: The infinite is the highest point of vastness.

context.previous: 日月者，明之極也；
context.next: 聖人者，道之極也。

translations.chinese: 聖人者，道之極也。
translations.literal: Sages are way extreme.
translations.idiomatic: Sages are the highest point of the Way.

context.previous: 無窮者，廣大之極也；

translations.chinese: 以財物為用，以貴賤為文，以多少為異，以隆殺為要。
translations.literal: Use wealth things as use, use noble base as pattern, use many few as different, use flourishing decline as essential.
translations.idiomatic: They use wealth and goods as function, noble and base as pattern, many and few as distinction, and flourishing and decline as the key.

context.next: 文貌繁，情欲省，禮之隆也；

translations.chinese: 文貌繁，情欲省，禮之隆也；
translations.literal: Pattern appearance abundant, feelings desires frugal, rites flourishing;
translations.idiomatic: When form and appearance are abundant and feeling and desire are restrained, rites are in their flourishing.

context.previous: 以財物為用，以貴賤為文，以多少為異，以隆殺為要。
context.next: 文貌省，情欲繁，禮之殺也；

translations.chinese: 文貌省，情欲繁，禮之殺也；
translations.literal: Pattern appearance frugal, feelings desires abundant, rites decline;
translations.idiomatic: When form and appearance are restrained and feeling and desire are abundant, rites are in decline.

context.previous: 文貌繁，情欲省，禮之隆也；
context.next: 文貌情欲相為內外表裏，并行而雜，禮之中流也。

translations.chinese: 文貌情欲相為內外表裏，并行而雜，禮之中流也。
translations.literal: Pattern appearance feelings desires mutually as inner outer surface lining, proceed together mixed, rites middle flow.
translations.idiomatic: When form and appearance, feeling and desire, serve as inner and outer, surface and lining, moving together and intermingled, rites are in their middle course.

context.previous: 文貌省，情欲繁，禮之殺也；
context.next: 君子上致其隆，下盡其殺，而中處其中。

translations.chinese: 君子上致其隆，下盡其殺，而中處其中。
translations.literal: Gentleman above reach its flourishing, below exhaust its decline, middle dwell in middle.
translations.idiomatic: The gentleman reaches the height of what is flourishing above, exhausts what is declining below, and dwells in the middle at the center.

context.previous: 文貌情欲相為內外表裏，并行而雜，禮之中流也。
context.next: 步驟馳騁廣騖不外，是以君子之性守宮庭也。

translations.chinese: 步驟馳騁廣騖不外，是以君子之性守宮庭也。
translations.literal: Steps paces gallop race broad unrestrained not outside, therefore gentleman nature guards palace court.
translations.idiomatic: Moving and ranging broadly without going outside it, this is why the gentleman's nature keeps to the palace court.

context.previous: 君子上致其隆，下盡其殺，而中處其中。
context.next: 人域是域，士君子也。

translations.chinese: 人域是域，士君子也。
translations.literal: Human domain this domain, scholar gentleman.
translations.idiomatic: The domain of humanity is the domain of the scholar-gentleman.

context.previous: 步驟馳騁廣騖不外，是以君子之性守宮庭也。
context.next: 外是，民也。

translations.chinese: 外是，民也。
translations.literal: Outside this, common people.
translations.idiomatic: Outside this is the common people.

context.previous: 人域是域，士君子也。
context.next: 於是中焉，房皇周浹，曲［直］得其次序，聖人也。

translations.chinese: 於是中焉，房皇周浹，曲［直］得其次序，聖人也。
translations.literal: Thus middle there, chamber grand complete cycle, curved straight obtain their sequence, sage person.
translations.idiomatic: Within this middle, the chambers are broad and complete, and curved and straight each obtain their proper order; this is a sage.

context.previous: 外是，民也。
context.next: 故厚者，禮之積也；

translations.chinese: 故厚者，禮之積也；
translations.literal: Therefore thick is rites accumulation;
translations.idiomatic: Therefore, the thick is the accumulation of rites.

context.previous: 於是中焉，房皇周浹，曲［直］得其次序，聖人也。
context.next: 大者，禮之廣也；

translations.chinese: 大者，禮之廣也；
translations.literal: Great is rites breadth;
translations.idiomatic: The great is the breadth of rites.

context.previous: 故厚者，禮之積也；
context.next: 高者，禮之隆也；

translations.chinese: 高者，禮之隆也；
translations.literal: High is rites flourishing;
translations.idiomatic: The high is the flourishing of rites.

context.previous: 大者，禮之廣也；
context.next: 明者，禮之盡也。

translations.chinese: 明者，禮之盡也。
translations.literal: Bright is rites exhaustion.
translations.idiomatic: The bright is the exhaustion of rites.

context.previous: 高者，禮之隆也；
